title: Realization square for one basic canonical generator
statement: Fix D,l,E,o,a and a recursive expression comparison satisfying RecursionLaws. For a BasicPair of independently prescribed system and ordinary ringed arrows s,r, on a common geometric admissible input K, and with the source completion map invertible, L(s) followed by the target comparison equals the source comparison followed by inverse source completion, r, and target completion. This concerns BasicPair generators only, with no CanonicalPair identity, composition or context closure.

source.place: Coefficient comparisons and inherited equations, expanded strict-system realization argument.

proof.text: Construct the ordinary coefficient map on every expression independently of the comparison family. The normalization theorem identifies its adjunction transpose, followed by the supplied comparison, with the actual expression completion map. This is proved by expression induction, using the quotient augmentations, adjoint-conjugate proper comparison, and the prescribed openNormalization equation.

For a forward canonical isomorphism use the ordinary canonical-iso square; derive the inverse square by cancellation of the two isomorphisms. The pull/direct-image and open unit/counit cases are the general mate unit/counit identities applied to the explicit child coefficient map. Use the separate ordinary proper/open, geometric exchange/projection, and compactification diagrams for the remaining constructors. Thus obtain the ordinary coefficient square by cases on BasicPair.

Transpose that coefficient square using naturality of the actual reduction/limit hom-set equivalence. The normalization equations identify the source and target transposes with completion followed by inverse comparison. The source transpose is invertible because the supplied source completion and comparison are invertible. Cancel it to obtain exactly the stated realization equation. No target completion inverse, coefficient evaluation faithfulness or closure under expression contexts is used.

proof_origin.place: J7: actual ordinary coefficient recursion, proved normalization by induction, generator case analysis, and categorical transposition/cancellation.

from.place: Coefficient-comparison sentence, canonical generators and finite outer contexts.

lean.statement:
theorem integralBasicGeneratorSquare (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (o : Operations l E) (a : AmbientModels l E o)
    (comparison : ExpressionRecursion.Comparisons l E D o)
    (laws : RecursionLaws l E D o a comparison)
    {I : Type u} [Finite I]
    {X : I → Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))}
    {W : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))}
    (e t : Expression _ I X W) (ge : e.geometric) (gt : t.geometric)
    (K : (e.domain l E o).FullSubcategory) (ht : t.domain l E o K.obj)
    (s : e.systemObj l E o ((inputReduction l E X).obj K.obj) ⟶
      t.systemObj l E o ((inputReduction l E X).obj K.obj))
    (r : e.ringedObj l E a.ringedModels K.obj ⟶
      t.ringedObj l E a.ringedModels K.obj)
    (h : BasicPair l E o a.compositors a.openComparisons a.canonicalBridge a.properOpen
      a.ringedModels a.ringedOpenComparisons a.ringedProperOpen
      ((inputReduction l E X).obj K.obj) K.obj e t s r)
    (he : IsIso (e.completionMap l E a.ringedModels K.obj)) :
    (coefficientSequenceLimit l E W.left).map s ≫
      (comparison t gt).hom.app ⟨K.obj, ht⟩ =
    (comparison e ge).hom.app K ≫
      @inv _ _ _ _ (e.completionMap l E a.ringedModels K.obj) he ≫
      r ≫ t.completionMap l E a.ringedModels K.obj
